files_changed.description: Add ImmediateSendRequest and ImmediateSendResponse Pydantic models. Do not modify existing NotificationCreateRequest or NotificationRecord.

additions.notes: No field validators needed. title and body are not constrained beyond being non-empty strings (Pydantic will reject missing fields automatically).
dispatched_at is server-captured application time, not read from DB. Pydantic will serialise it as ISO-8601.

files_changed.description: Add send_immediate() method to NotificationService. Do not modify existing create(), cancel(), or replace() methods.

steps: 1. Query notifications.device WHERE device_id='default'; if no row raise NoDefaultDeviceError
5. Call send_fcm_message(token=fcm_token, notification_id=notification_id, title=payload.title, body=payload.body, label='', deep_link=''); if raises, raise FCMDispatchError(original_exception)

6. INSERT INTO notifications.notification (id, source, fire_at, title, body, label, deep_link, fcm_token, status) VALUES (notification_id, payload.source, NULL, payload.title, payload.body, '', '', fcm_token, 'dispatched')

new_exceptions.description: Raised when notifications.device has no row for device_id='default'.
Raised when send_fcm_message() raises. Wraps the original exception as cause.

files_changed.description: Add POST /notifications/send route. Do not modify existing routes.

handler: On NoDefaultDeviceError: return api_error(code='NO_DEFAULT_DEVICE', message='No default device registered. Open AtlasPhone to register an FCM token.', status=503)
On FCMDispatchError: return api_error(code='FCM_DISPATCH_FAILED', message='FCM dispatch failed. The notification was not delivered.', status=502)

files_changed.route_ordering_note: POST /notifications/send must be registered BEFORE POST /notifications/{notification_id}/replace to avoid path ambiguity. In FastAPI, static path segments ('send') take priority over path parameters when registered first. Verify route order in the file.

files_changed.description: Migration to make label, deep_link nullable and fire_at nullable in notifications.notification. Safe to run on a live table; existing rows are unaffected (they already have non-null values in these columns).
content_summary: ALTER TABLE notifications.notification ALTER COLUMN fire_at DROP NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE notifications.notification ALTER COLUMN label DROP NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE notifications.notification ALTER COLUMN label SET DEFAULT '';
ALTER TABLE notifications.notification ALTER COLUMN deep_link DROP NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE notifications.notification ALTER COLUMN deep_link SET DEFAULT '';

no_new_files: No new modules or packages are created. All additions are extensions to existing files.
implementation_notes: Do not import FCMDispatchError or NoDefaultDeviceError in router until they are defined in service.py.
The POST /notifications/send route returns status_code=200, not 201, because the notification is already dispatched — there is no pending state.
dispatched_at in the response is the datetime captured BEFORE the INSERT, not read back from Postgres. Do not add a dispatched_at column to the schema.
The fire_at column being NULL in immediate-send rows means the APScheduler dispatch job (WHERE fire_at <= NOW()) will silently ignore them — no code change to dispatch_job.py needed.
Run the migration (10_schema.sql) against the live container before running tests.
